item.description: Residents of the small English village of Barnham voted on Saturday in a symbolic referendum to leave the UK, in protest against government plans to house 931 asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base – more than the village’s own population of 584. item.description: Por sexto sábado consecutivo, miles de personas volvieron a las calles de Francia para exigir mejores salarios, servicios públicos más fuertes y mejores condiciones de estudio. En París, sindicatos, estudiantes y representantes de los "chalecos amarillos" marcharon juntos en una jornada que forma parte de una movilización europea por el derecho a la vivienda y contra el aumento del costo de vida. item.description: Colombia conmemora diez años del histórico acuerdo entre el Estado y la ahora desmovilizada guerrilla de las FARC. Sin embargo, en los tres gobiernos que siguieron a la firma, los avances en su implementación han sido modestos y ahora el enfoque es de lucha frontal antiterrorista. Adrianus Koetsenruijter, enviado especial de la Unión Europea para el proceso de paz en esta nación, explica en France 24 algunas luces y sombras del pacto diseñado para poner fin a décadas de conflicto. item.title: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations
item.description: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal, ten years after talks began.The agreement removes almost all tariffs between the EU and Southeast Asia's biggest economy: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it means access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear, and it arrives just before its current EU trade preferences end on the 1st of January. To discuss the deal Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs in Indonesia joined us on the programme. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: 'Worst Ever' COP Summit?
item.description: Is this the worst COP summit on record? With limited political leadership, no official US delegation and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, questions are being raised about the effectiveness of the climate negotiations. Juan Carlos Beldsoe, a former White House climate adviser under Bill Clinton, described the process as labyrinthine and ultimately dispiriting.
